why: EFFECT: “Your unit’s ranged attacks that target a unit within 9" have +1 AP.” The footnote is mod {kind:'ranged', when:'Your Shooting phase, vs targets within 9"', note:'+1 AP'}. I ran app.html stratModLines with this mod and the Kustom Dakka one. It prints the label “Stratagems · Shoota Boyz · Your Shooting phase”, then “1CP +1 AP vs targets within 9" (Glowin’ Dakka)”. The condition starts with “vs”, so it is joined with a space, not a comma. If the detachment’s footnotes had different phases, it would print “1CP +1 AP, Your Shooting phase, vs targets within 9"”, which says the same thing. Checks: (1) The effect matches: “+1 AP” is the rule’s own words, not changed into “AP -1” or “improve AP”. (2) The attacks match: kind:'ranged' means the line only appears with the unit’s ranged weapons, and the rule covers only “ranged attacks”. (3) The condition matches: “vs targets within 9"” means attacks against a target unit within 9", which is the rule’s “that target a unit within 9"”. Nothing is added: no visibility, closest-target or once-per-phase limit. Nothing is lost. (4) The phase is right: WHEN is “Your Shooting phase, when a friendly ORKS INFANTRY unit is selected to shoot”. It is shown once on the detachment label. Leaving out “when selected to shoot” matches the Kustom Dakka line, and 1CP matches cp:1. (5) Which units get it: TARGET “That ORKS INFANTRY unit” comes from needs {all:['Faction: Orks','Infantry']} through eligible(), so the line only appears on ORKS INFANTRY sheets. Ambiguity: the rule does not say what the 9" is measured from. The usual reading is the shooting unit (“your unit”). The footnote sits under this unit’s ranged weapons, so it reads the same way and is no vaguer than the rule. The old wording “target within 9"” had the same open point. Changing “a unit” to “targets” does not change what the rule means.
